[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes, quick intros - I'm Maya from Redwood, Jordan is our SE - Jordan you want to intro?
[00:08] Jordan: yep, hi all, SE at Redwood, I'll cover technical bits, perf and onboarding.
[00:12] Laura: Laura here, procurement, handling contracting and pricing approvals.
[00:16] Daniel: Daniel, legal counsel, I'll be focusing on the MSA and DPA.
[00:19] Ravi: Ravi, VP Eng, interested in latency, private deployment and onboarding timeline.

[00:30] Maya: great, agenda — go over the MSA/DPA redlines, SLA asks, pricing timeline, and next steps for onboarding. We also uploaded MSA_v3_redline.pdf and Security_Packet.zip in the calendar — links in chat.
[00:45] Laura: yes saw those, thanks. procurement wants to know how soon we can get the MSA acceptable to our legal so we can move to PO and pilot.
[00:52] Daniel: quick callouts from our side: indemnity caps, data residency for PII, audit rights, and sub-processor list. also need to confirm SOC 2 scope and pen test recency.
[01:12] Maya: understood. for SOC 2 we provided report as of 2026-03 and our pen test summary, both in the security packet. we can add explicit language about audit logs and retention. on indemnity, can you share example wording you prefer?
[01:30] Daniel: typical is mutual limited indemnity, with carveouts for willful misconduct. also want to ensure we don't have open-ended liability for model hallucinations — language around misuse.
[01:45] Jordan: quick technical note — for PII handling we support VPC-private deployments and customer-managed KMS. if you want keys in HSM we integrate with common providers, we can list options.
[02:05] Ravi: that KMS bit is critical — we will require customer-managed keys for production. also, do you support on-prem full-stack?
[02:15] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem and VPC options. we'll include explicit deployment options in the DPA appendix.
[02:24] Laura: SLA side — procurement needs a clear uptime SLA and also some latency SLOs for API responses, at least for critical endpoints. what's typical?
[02:34] Jordan: our Dedicated customers often get 99.9% uptime SLA for the serving runtime. for latency we publish P50/P95 and can offer 99th pct latency objectives for the dedicated pool, but exact numbers depend on model, sequence length and batch config. we can propose targets in the SLA appendix.
[02:54] Daniel: we need clear remedies — credits or termination rights if SLA violated over rolling periods.
[03:05] Maya: standard is service credits. termination is usually for repeated SLA breaches, we can include a 3-strike remediation process.
[03:15] Daniel: okay we'll review that.

[03:40] Laura: pricing — procurement needs the final pricing matrix for pilot vs prod, plus seat/throughput rates. we have a procurement window mid-June; need approvals by 6/18 to get Q3 budget.
[03:52] Maya: we'll update pricing worksheet with pilot discount and dedicated pool rates. can we get an internal approver list and target sign date?
[04:00] Laura: yes I'll share approvers. aiming for 6/18 sign but legal must sign earlier ideally.

[04:20] Jordan: on the technical onboarding, we'll provision a pilot Dedicated pool for you, run a perf benchmark. quick note: our KV cache and prefix caching dramatically change latency profiles; we'll simulate your traffic. please send a representative workload.
[04:35] Ravi: we'll prepare a sample of 10k calls/day with typical prompt sizes, and send via secure link.
[04:42] Jordan: great. i'll plan a 2-hour run and share results. expect P95 figures and token cost estimates.

[05:05] Daniel: back to DPA — sub-processors list? we need names and locales.
[05:12] Maya: yes we'll send the current sub-processor list; most are in NA and EU. we can add contractual language if you need to restrict certain regions.
[05:23] Daniel: good. also audit rights — we need to be able to annually audit certain controls or get third-party attestation.
[05:30] Maya: we can offer SOC2 report and contractual audit cooperation; full on-site audits are rare but let's capture expectations.

[06:00] Laura: invoice & PO — will Redwood accept a net-45?
[06:06] Maya: typical is net-30 but we can be flexible for enterprise deals; we'll note net-45 request and get finance confirmation.
[06:12] Laura: thanks.

[06:30] Daniel: about data residency, we require EU-resident data for EU customers — can you pin region?
[06:36] Jordan: yes, routing by region is supported; we can pin model serving to EU regions and avoid cross-border processing for those tenants.
[06:45] Ravi: also curious about fallback models and graceful degradation if capacity is constrained — does Redwood have automatic fallbacks?
[06:52] Jordan: yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or lower-cost tiers; we'll document behavior in the SLA appendix. note that model variant fallbacks may change output characteristics.

[07:10] Maya: i'm going to recap deliverables — we'll share MSA v3 redline, DPA with KMS and region appendix, SLA appendix with proposed uptime and latency targets, and pricing worksheet updated with pilot and dedicated pool rates. Jordan will schedule the perf pilot.
[07:25] Laura: looks good. legal (Daniel) will send redlines. procurement (me) will align approver list and timeline.

[07:40] Daniel: one more legal nuance — data deletion and retention periods; we want the ability to request deletion and a cert of deletion.
[07:48] Jordan: we support data deletion APIs for logs and can provide attestations of deletion, will include process in DPA.

[08:10] Maya: perfect. any blockers to moving forward now?
[08:15] Laura: main item is legal redlines and procurement sign-off timeline — if we get MSA updated quickly and legal is ok, we can move to PO.
[08:24] Maya: we'll target sending the updated docs by Tuesday 2026-06-02.

[08:40] Ravi: timeline for onboarding — how long from signed MSA to pilot start?
[08:45] Jordan: typically 2-3 weeks to provision dedicated pool and run initial tuning and the perf run — less if we use hosted pilot. we'll include options.

[09:02] Laura: ok that's acceptable.

[09:20] Maya: any other questions?
[09:25] Daniel: none for now.
[09:30] Maya: great, we'll capture action items and send calendar invites for the technical deep dive and perf pilot. thanks all.

End of transcript.
